title: Pete Carmichael Discusses Win Over the Ravens
headline: DJ Moore returned from injury and the coordinator said he played fast and gave the offense energy. Drops were shrugged off, and Minnesota's blitz-heavy defense is next.
summary: Carmichael said the offense was not efficient enough in the run game in the first half and missed some throw-and-catch chances. He said the players executed better in the second half and that the coaches had to be better early as well. He praised DJ Moore's return, saying Moore played fast and brought energy to the receiver group. On the drops, he said he has no concerns but that they can't keep happening, and he took some blame for putting the ball in a worse spot on a few throws. He credited the offensive line's protection plan, including chips and nudges, for keeping Trey Hendrickson from wrecking the game. He said the team's strong fourth-down numbers come from Joe Brady's confidence and a week of preparation on calls and tendencies. He called the Vikings a great defense that will bring many challenges and said the line and Josh Allen have communicated well. The conversation about the new right tackle did not make clear who he was talking about. He also said the team has a third quarterback option it feels good about and deferred further detail to Brady.

injuries.detail: Played in the win over the Ravens in his return to action. Carmichael said he played fast and played really well.

A reporter asked about a new right tackle and a lineman next to him who has played less, called 'Tyler'. Carmichael said only that he played well. It's unclear who was meant and whether Spencer Brown (limited, ankle) was affected.

signals.claim: DJ Moore is back in the offense and playing at a high level after his return.
signals.note: A clean return with praise for his speed and energy suggests he should keep a full role in the passing game.

topics.detail: The run game was not efficient enough early and some catchable throws were missed. The offense executed better after halftime, and the coaches said they need to be better early.
Carmichael has no concerns about the drops, saying they are plays the team must make. He said some throws could have been better placed, and the drops can't continue.
The week's plan covered which side Hendrickson would line up on and where to use chips or nudges. Carmichael thought the offensive line did a great job, and Hendrickson had no sack and one QB hit.

Carmichael credited Joe Brady's confidence as play caller and a week of preparation on calls by field position. He said the offense must be ready for Brady to go for it on fourth down. He admitted third down was not great against Baltimore.
The field-goal drive after the third-and-25 and the clock management were planned during the week. The staff discussed in advance how many seconds to leave and which look to expect.

Carmichael expects a great, blitz-heavy defense with many challenges. He credited the offensive line and Josh Allen for communicating well on protections, and said pressure looks can limit how much the line can shift protection.
The team has a third quarterback option it feels good about. It would also consider a running back or receiver taking snaps. Carmichael deferred to Brady for details.

title: WATCH: Brian Angelichio Media Availability (Nov. 2)
headline: Steelers OC Brian Angelichio says the run game is humming, but the dropback game and red-zone offense need work. Germie Bernard is earning trust with Aaron Rodgers, and DK Metcalf's confidence is not a concern despite a costly play.
summary: Angelichio was asked about the league's most efficient rushing attack and said the team is still looking for balance in the dropback game. He pointed to concepts and timing with the quarterback's feet as the areas to fix over the next two days. He credited the interior line for the run success, singling out Zach Frazier's calls and the guards' physical play, and explained that trap runs are mainly a tool against upfield, penetrating four-man fronts on third and long. He admitted the red-zone offense has to improve and said everything is under review, including play selection, run/pass balance and checks. He praised Germie Bernard's growing comfort and trust with Rodgers, his run-after-catch ability and his toughness, and expects his role to grow with more playing time. Michael Pittman is rehabbing, attending meetings and taking part in game planning, with no return timeline given. Eli Heidenreich is getting reps and developing on the look team. On DK Metcalf, he said a play from the game is one he'd love to have back, but the team has not lost confidence in him.

injuries.detail: Attacking his rehab and in all meetings and game-plan sessions. A reporter said he was running today. Angelichio gave no return timeline and said the medical staff handles that.

signals.claim: Bernard will see an increasing target share from Aaron Rodgers as he plays more and the trust grows.
signals.note: With the receiver injuries, Bernard is becoming a trusted target, and his strength after the catch gives him a rising role.
signals.quote: He's a tough tackle. He's got good explosion.

signals.claim: Metcalf remains a featured part of the offense despite a costly play in the Browns game.
signals.note: The coach is backing him publicly, so there is no sign of a role reduction, but weekly volume may vary.
signals.quote: we have not lost confidence in him at all.

signals.claim: Pittman is progressing in rehab and is being kept current on the game plan for an eventual return.
signals.note: He is not yet cleared, and no timetable was given, so keep him on your watch list.
signals.quote: we can't wait to get him back out there.

signals.claim: Heidenreich is progressing on the look team and gaining run-game skills and reads.
signals.note: He is developing, but there is no sign of an offensive role yet, so he is a stash-level name at best.
signals.quote: he's done a great job on the look team.

signals.claim: The dropback game needs better timing and consistency, which the coaches will work on this week.
signals.note: The passing offense trails the run game, which caps Rodgers' fantasy ceiling until the timing issues improve.
signals.quote: it's a great job by Aaron.

signals.claim: Frazier will keep setting protections and run-blocking assignments for an efficient rushing attack.
signals.note: A strong interior line supports the run game and the Steelers' rushing production.
signals.quote: Frege does his phenomenal job as anybody I've been around

topics.detail: Pittsburgh has the league's most efficient rushing attack, which Angelichio credits to the interior line's combination blocks, handling of movement fronts and physical play from Frazier, Brock Hoffman and Mason McCormick.
Trap runs are a situational tool against upfield, penetrating four-man fronts, especially on third and long. They are not as good against reading defenders or five-man fronts.
Angelichio acknowledged the red-zone offense has to improve. The staff will review play selection, run/pass balance and pre-snap checks over the next two days.
He said some issues from the mini-bye self-scout have been addressed, but more cleanup is needed, and the staff will review it again this week.
Play-calling is collaborative: Mike McCarthy and Rodgers talk directly, and the staff coordinates between series on sequencing.
